questions.questionText: A rectangular block is cut by 2 plane(s) parallel to its length-breadth face, 2 plane(s) parallel to its breadth-height face and 1 plane(s) parallel to its length-height face. How many pieces are formed?
questions.explanation: Slices in the three directions are 3, 3 and 2. Pieces = 3 × 3 × 2 = 18.

questions.questionText: A rectangular block is cut by 2 plane(s) parallel to its length-breadth face, 2 plane(s) parallel to its breadth-height face and 2 plane(s) parallel to its length-height face. How many pieces are formed?
questions.explanation: Slices in the three directions are 3, 3 and 3. Pieces = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.

questions.questionText: A rectangular block is cut by 3 plane(s) parallel to its length-breadth face, 1 plane(s) parallel to its breadth-height face and 2 plane(s) parallel to its length-height face. How many pieces are formed?
questions.explanation: Slices in the three directions are 4, 2 and 3. Pieces = 4 × 2 × 3 = 24.

questions.questionText: A rectangular block is cut by 1 plane(s) parallel to its length-breadth face, 3 plane(s) parallel to its breadth-height face and 3 plane(s) parallel to its length-height face. How many pieces are formed?
questions.explanation: Slices in the three directions are 2, 4 and 4. Pieces = 2 × 4 × 4 = 32.

questions.questionText: A rectangular block is cut by 4 plane(s) parallel to its length-breadth face, 2 plane(s) parallel to its breadth-height face and 1 plane(s) parallel to its length-height face. How many pieces are formed?
questions.explanation: Slices in the three directions are 5, 3 and 2. Pieces = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum number of pieces a cube can be divided into using exactly 3 plane cuts (rearranging pieces not allowed)?
questions.explanation: Each plane can at most double the pieces in the best case: 3 mutually perpendicular planes through the centre give 2×2×2 = 8 pieces.
questions.shortcut: 3 planes in 3 directions: 2×2×2.

questions.questionText: A cube is cut by 6 planes, 2 parallel to each pair of opposite faces, with all cuts equally spaced. How many pieces are formed?
questions.explanation: Each direction is cut into 3 slices: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.

questions.questionText: A 4 × 4 × 4 cube made of unit cubes is painted on all faces and dismantled. If all the unit cubes with at least one painted face are removed and the rest are glued into one solid, what is its shape and number of cubes?
questions.explanation: Unpainted cubes form the inner (4−2)³ = 2³ block: a 2 × 2 × 2 cube of 8 cubes.
questions.shortcut: Inner block is (n−2) per side.

questions.questionText: A cube of side 10 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. What is the total number of painted small faces on all the unit cubes together?
questions.explanation: Total painted area = 6 × 10² = 600 cm², so 600 unit faces are painted.
questions.shortcut: Painted faces = 6n².

questions.questionText: A 5 cm cube painted on all faces is cut into 1 cm cubes. If the cubes having exactly three painted faces and the cubes having no painted faces are removed, how many cubes remain?
questions.explanation: Total 125; three-face cubes = 8; unpainted = 27. Remaining = 125 − 8 − 27 = 90.
questions.shortcut: Remaining = edges + faces = 36 + 54 = 90.

questions.questionText: A cube is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. The number of cubes with exactly one painted face is 6 times the number with no painted face. What is the side of the cube in cm?
questions.explanation: 6(n−2)² = 6(n−2)³ → n−2 = 1 → n = 3. Check: 6 cubes with one face, 1 with none.

questions.questionText: In a painted cube cut into unit cubes, exactly 24 unit cubes have two painted faces. How many unit cubes have exactly one painted face?
questions.shortcut: Find n from 12(n−2), then apply 6(n−2)².

questions.questionText: In a painted cube cut into unit cubes, exactly 36 unit cubes have two painted faces. How many unit cubes have exactly one painted face?
questions.shortcut: Find n from 12(n−2), then apply 6(n−2)².

questions.questionText: In a painted cube cut into unit cubes, exactly 48 unit cubes have two painted faces. How many unit cubes have exactly one painted face?
questions.shortcut: Find n from 12(n−2), then apply 6(n−2)².
